narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'serve the LORD with fear' (abad) - service demanded of rulers who have just been plotting revolt (v1-3). Type (102) is volition: not a felt state nor a settled trait but an act of the will, service chosen, the interior turned from rebellion to submission. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring for the turn - it reports the summons, not what supplies it, resting the weight on the act of willing. Seat (104) resolves to none: the service is not lodged in a named inner organ but held by the persons as such, the whole self reoriented rather than a faculty switched on. Bearer (105) is 'the kings' (inferred, to_span 276502): the interior addressed is that of the earth's rulers and judges warned in v10 - the once-conspiring will now told to serve. Operation (106), the core event, is 'the prudent response: to serve the LORD in fear - reverent submission replacing revolt': the movement is a turn from casting off the cords (v3) to bending under them. Target (107) is 'reverent-service' (inferred, to_span 276502): the operation aims at the reverent service itself, submission as the fitting posture. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked beyond the fear already carried in the sense; the summons stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows the service, and no downstream outcome is booked - the reading holds the commanded posture, not its result. Coupling (112) is 'serve-in-fear' (inferred, to_span 276502): the binding registered is the weld of service to fear, the two inseparable - not glad service but service under dread, the fear the fitting answer of the once-rebellious. Prohibition (113) is absent: this is a positive charge, not a forbidding. Discovery (114) names it: v11 'SERVE the LORD with FEAR' - the interior reorients from casting-off to serving; fear here is the fitting posture of the once-rebellious before the king. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing bearing the ruler is charged to hold. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the reorientation sits inside, a condition of the inner life. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the rebellious kings' will is turned to serve the LORD, welded to fear and reported without degree - reverent submission replacing revolt, lodged wholly within as the changed posture of the once-defiant.
narratives.story: The psalm has just shown kings and rulers plotting to throw off God's rule, straining to snap the cords that bind them. Then comes the turn: serve the Lord with fear. Service here is a decision of the will - the rebel choosing to bend. It is aimed squarely at the very rulers who had been conspiring; their defiant hearts are told to submit. And the service is inseparable from fear: this is not glad, easy service but the reverent dread that fits those who once resisted and now bow. The passage does not say where this change of heart is meant to come from, and it names no reward for it; it simply issues the summons and leaves the turning to the will. What it pictures is a whole inner reorientation - from casting off God's rule to serving under it, from revolt to reverent submission.
narratives.variation_note: One of four readings of 'serve' (abad) in this family, and the difference across them is the finding. Here at Psa 2:11 service is VOLITION - the once-rebellious kings' will turned to reverent submission, welded to FEAR (serve-in-fear) as the fitting answer of the defiant. It differs from Psa 22:30 (#2), where service is carried forward in time by unborn posterity; from Psa 100:2 (#3), where it is present, glad, corporate worship coupled with gladness and singing; and sharply from Psa 106:36 (#4), the descent reading, where the same verb names service turned to idols that snared the people. This reading's distinctive is the pivot from revolt to submission under dread.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'kiss the Son' (nashaq) - an act of homage commanded of the same rulers, submission given outward, bodily form. Type (102) is volition: an act of the will, the kiss chosen, the once-conspiring interior electing to do homage. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring for the homage - it reports the command, not its origin. Seat (104) resolves to none: the kiss is not lodged in a named inner organ; it is the person's act, the whole self bending, not a faculty engaged. Bearer (105) is 'the kings' (inferred, to_span 276507): the interior addressed is again the earth's rulers, the conspirators of v1-3 now told to pay court. Operation (106) is 'the act of homage: to kiss the Son, submission embodied, lest wrath be kindled': the movement is the interior submission taking outward, physical form under threat of anger. Target (107) is 'homage' (inferred, to_span 276507): the operation aims at the homage itself - the kiss as the enacted submission owed the king. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the command stands bare. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree of the homage is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream result is booked - the reading holds the commanded act, not its outcome. Coupling (112) is 'kiss-the-son' (inferred, to_span 276507): the binding registered is the homage itself, act and object fused - the kiss and the one kissed inseparable. Prohibition (113) is absent: this is a positive charge. Discovery (114) names it: v12 'KISS the Son, lest he be angry' - the interior submission takes outward form; the once-conspiring will now does homage. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of submission the ruler is charged to hold. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - though the kiss is a bodily act, the reading lodges it as a condition of the inner life, the submission that the outward gesture enacts. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the rebellious kings' will elects to do homage, kissing the Son in embodied submission under the threat of kindled wrath - an act of will whose inner substance, held within as an ib-state, is the surrender of the once-defiant.
narratives.story: Right after the kings are told to serve with fear, the psalm presses further: kiss the Son, or he will be angry. The kiss is homage - the outward gesture by which a subject pays court to his king. It is chosen; the conspirators of the opening lines must now decide to bend and give it. What the passage cares about is not the lips but the surrender behind them: the kiss is the inner submission made visible, and it is given under the shadow of wrath quickly kindled. The plotting heart that wanted to be free is now told to come and do reverence. The text does not explain where such a change of will comes from, nor does it dwell on what follows; it simply commands the act - the once-defiant ruler bowing to kiss the one he had defied.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'posterity shall serve and proclaim' (abad) - service projected into the future, a coming generation serving God. Type (102) is volition: an act of the will, service the future interior will render, not a felt state. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked for the service - the reading reports its extension forward, not its origin. Seat (104) resolves to none: the service is not lodged in an inner organ but held by the generations as such. Bearer (105) is 'posterity' (inferred, to_span 275757): the interior in view is that of the unborn - the seed yet to come, read from the vindicated sufferer's turn to the future in v30-31. Operation (106) is 'posterity shall serve God; it shall be told of the Lord to a coming generation, who proclaim his righteousness - the praise carried forward in time': the movement is service handed down, becoming testimony to the not-yet-born. Target (107) is 'generational-service' (inferred, to_span 275757): the operation aims at service that spans generations, the worship inherited and passed on. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked beyond the proclaiming already in the operation. Coupling (112) is 'posterity-serves' (inferred, to_span 275757): the binding registered is service welded to lineage - the serving inseparable from the succession of generations that carry it. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v30-31 'Posterity shall SERVE him... they shall PROCLAIM his righteousness to a people yet unborn' - the operation extends the vindication into the future; unborn generations will serve and tell. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the coming people. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the service is a condition of the inner life, held within each generation even as it issues in proclamation. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, service is projected forward onto the unborn, welded to the succession of generations - a willed serving that becomes testimony, carrying the vindicated one's cause into a future it will not see, lodged within each coming interior as its inherited posture.
narratives.story: The long psalm of suffering has turned to praise, and near its end the singer looks past his own lifetime. Those who come after will serve God, he says, and the story of the Lord will be told to a generation not yet born. Service here reaches into the future: it is something the unborn will choose to render, handed down like an inheritance from parent to child. What the sufferer has lived through will not be forgotten; it will become the testimony that a whole line of people carries forward, serving and proclaiming God's righteousness to those who have not yet drawn breath. The passage does not say what starts this or where it ends; it simply sees service outrunning death, passed from one generation to the next as the settled way the coming people will live before God.
narratives.variation_note: Second of four 'serve' (abad) readings. Its distinctive is time: here service is projected onto unborn POSTERITY and welded to the succession of generations, becoming testimony carried forward. It differs from Psa 2:11 (#1), the rebel kings' present submission under fear; from Psa 100:2 (#3), the congregation's present glad service; and from Psa 106:36 (#4), the descent reading of service turned to idols. Where #1 stresses a change of will and #3 stresses joy, this reading stresses inheritance - service outliving the one who first rendered it.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'wash my hands in innocence' (rachats) - a cleansing done as approach to worship. Type (102) is volition: an act of the will, the self choosing to purify itself before drawing near. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the deliberate act, not its origin, though the whole psalm has rehearsed the psalmist's integrity and separation from evildoers (v4-5). Seat (104) resolves to none: the washing is not lodged in an inner organ; it is the person's act, the whole self made ready rather than a faculty engaged. Bearer (105) is 'the psalmist' (inferred, to_span 276164): the interior in view is David's, the one who has walked in integrity (v1) and now approaches the altar. Operation (106) is 'the self washes its hands in innocence and goes around the altar - approaching worship with a cleansed conscience': the movement is a deliberate purification that clears the way to God's presence. Target (107) is 'ritual-purity' (inferred, to_span 276164): the operation aims at cleanness - a purity that is at once outward gesture and inward innocence. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the act stands plainly stated. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree of the washing is scored, nothing further narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked - the reading holds the act of preparation, not a measured result. Coupling (112) is 'wash-in-innocence' (inferred, to_span 276164): the binding registered is the weld of washing to innocence - the outward rinse and the inward cleanness inseparable, so the gesture means nothing apart from the conscience it enacts. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v6 'I WASH my hands in INNOCENCE and go around your altar, O LORD' - a deliberate purification before drawing near; clean conscience as the ticket to the altar. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the worshipper who comes clean. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the washing is lodged as a condition of the inner life, innocence the true substance the hands enact. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist deliberately washes his hands in innocence and circles the altar, welding the outward rinse to inward cleanness - a willed preparation for worship whose real content, held within, is the clean conscience that alone may draw near.
narratives.story: This psalm is a plea from a man sure of his own integrity, one who has kept away from liars and evildoers. As he comes to worship, he pictures himself washing his hands in innocence and walking around God's altar. The washing is chosen, a deliberate act of getting ready to draw near. But the water is not really the point: the outward rinse stands for an inward cleanness, and the two cannot be pulled apart - the gesture means nothing without the clear conscience behind it. He is saying, in effect, that a person comes to God's presence clean, and that the clean conscience is what earns the approach. The passage does not trace where this innocence comes from or what it yields; it simply shows the worshipper preparing himself, hands and heart together, before he circles the altar.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'utterly bowed down, mourning all day' (avah) - the body bent low, not in worship but under grief. Read without valence-filtering, this is prostration in its dark form: the same folding of the frame that homage requires, here forced by anguish. Type (102) is state: not a chosen act but a condition the sufferer is in - bowed, prostrate, mourning. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring for the bowing here, though the psalm has just traced it to sin and God's arrows (v3-4); the row reports the state, not its cause. Seat (104) resolves to none: the bowing is not lodged in a named inner organ; it grips the whole frame, the person as such folded rather than a faculty struck. Bearer (105) is 'the psalmist' (inferred, to_span 277984): the interior in view is the sufferer's, crushed by guilt and disease across the whole psalm. Operation (106) is 'the self is utterly bowed down and prostrate; all the day it goes about mourning - a whole day bent under grief': the movement is the interior's mourning bending the body, grief made posture. Target (107) is 'prostration' (inferred, to_span 277984): what the state resolves to is prostration itself - the being pressed to the ground, not toward any object of homage but under its own weight of sorrow. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked beyond the 'utterly' and 'all the day' carried in the sense; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent as booked rows: no separate degree, narrowing, or downstream outcome is filed, though the 'utterly... all day' already signals extremity within the sense. Coupling (112) is 'bowed-and-mourning' (inferred, to_span 277984): the binding registered is the weld of bowing to mourning - the bent body and the grieving interior inseparable, the posture being simply the grief made visible. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v6 'I am utterly BOWED DOWN and prostrate; all the day I go about MOURNING' - the operation is the body folded by grief; the interior's mourning bends the whole frame. Role (115) is characteristic: read as a standing condition across this psalm of affliction, not a passing stoop. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state - the bowing is lodged as a condition of the inner life, mourning the substance the bent body enacts. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the sufferer's whole frame is bent to the ground all day long, welded to mourning - prostration not as homage offered but as grief's own posture, the interior's anguish pressing the body low and holding it there.
narratives.story: Here the same low, bent posture that belongs to worship appears in its darkest form. This is a man wrecked by guilt and sickness - God's arrows have sunk into him, his wounds fester, his sins weigh like a load too heavy to carry. And under all of it his body folds: he is utterly bowed down, prostrate, going about in mourning the whole day long. He has not chosen to bow; grief has bent him. The stoop of his body and the sorrow in his heart are one and the same thing - the anguish inside made visible in a frame pressed to the ground. The passage does not, at this point, dwell on the cause or the cure; it simply shows a person crushed low and kept there, mourning without pause. It is prostration not as reverence given to anyone, but as the shape that unbearable grief forces on a human body.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'bow down / do homage' (shachah) - the very word carried through this family for worship, here turned toward a human king. Type (102) is action: a doing, the bride's act of reverence, not a felt state. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked for the homage - the reading reports the charge, not its origin. Seat (104) resolves to none: the bowing is not lodged in an inner organ; it is the bride's act, the whole self bending, not a faculty engaged. Bearer (105) is 'the bride' (inferred, to_span 278898): the interior in view is the queen's, the daughter told in v10 to forget her people and her father's house. Operation (106) is 'bow / do homage': the event is the reverent bending itself. Target (107) is 'the king (her lord)' (inferred, to_span 278898): the homage is aimed at the royal bridegroom - and here is the sharp difference from the rest of the family: the object is not God but a man, 'since he is your lord.' Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the charge stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree of the homage is scored, nothing narrows it, and no downstream outcome is booked. Coupling (112) is none: unusually for this family, the reading registers no binding to a companion act - the homage stands alone, not welded to praise or thanks or fear. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: 'Since he is your lord, BOW (shachah) to him' - the bride's homage to the king; shachah, elsewhere the word of worship, here the reverent submission owed to her lord, the posture of the queen toward the king. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing bearing of the bride toward her husband-king. Locus (116) is external:person - and this is the decisive finding: unlike the worship readings whose reference-point is God or the ib-state, here the bowing is directed OUTWARD to another human being; the homage's whole orientation is toward a person. The full process: from no booked source, no organ-seat, and no companion coupling, the bride does homage to her royal lord - the same bending that belongs to God's worship now owed to a man, its locus wholly external, a reverent submission of wife to husband-king rather than creature to Creator.
narratives.story: In this royal wedding song the word usually reserved for worshipping God is turned toward a man. The bride, newly told to leave behind her own people and her father's house, is urged to bow to the king - because, the poet says, he is her lord. It is the same low gesture of reverence that elsewhere belongs to God, but here its whole direction is toward another human being: a wife's homage to her husband-king. And it stands by itself, not tied to singing or thanks or fear as worship of God so often is; it is simply reverent submission, given to a person. The passage does not explain where the impulse comes from or what it produces; it just names the posture - the queen bowing to the king she now belongs to. The striking thing is precisely that this bending points outward to a man, not upward to God.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'worship / bow down' (shachah) - 'all the earth worships you.' Type (102) is action: a doing, the whole earth's act of homage. Source (103) here carries a real value and is a span-resolved pair (from_span 281344 to_span 281335): 'before God's awesome deeds (v3).' This is the only worship reading in the family that books a named spring - the homage is drawn out by the sight of God's mighty acts, worship as response, not self-generated. Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the earth as such. Bearer (105) is 'all the earth' (inferred, to_span 281344): the interior in view is universal - every land, the whole creation turned worshipper. Operation (106) is 'worship / bow down': the event is the bending of all the earth before God. Target (107) is 'God' (inferred, to_span 281344): the homage is aimed at God himself. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) carries a value and is a span-resolved pair (from_span 281344 to_span 281345): 'paired with singing praises to his name' - the worship is welded to song; bowing and singing move together as one act. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: 'All the earth WORSHIPS (shachah) you and sings praises to you' - universal homage before God's awesome deeds; shachah here the bowing of all creation to God, worship as the whole earth's fitting posture. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of all the earth. Locus (116) is external:god - the worship's reference-point is God, directed outward and upward to him. The full process: drawn out by the sight of God's awesome deeds, the whole earth bows before him and sings praise to his name - worship here traced, uniquely in the family, to a named source, welded to song, and directed wholly to God as the fitting response of all creation to what it has seen him do.
narratives.story: This psalm calls the whole earth to shout for joy to God, and at its heart is a picture of every land bowing before him. What makes this moment stand out is that it names why they bow: it is the sight of God's awesome deeds, his great power, that draws the homage out of them. Worship here is a response - not something people work up in themselves, but the natural answer of those who have seen what God has done. And the bowing does not come alone; it moves together with song, the whole earth kneeling and singing praise to his name in one act. This is worship as the fitting posture of all creation before its God: not commanded coldly, but pulled from the world by the greatness of his works.
narratives.variation_note: First of nine readings of 'worship' (shachah) in this family. Its distinctive is that it alone books a SOURCE - the worship is drawn out 'before God's awesome deeds' (v3) - making this the one reading where the homage is explicitly traced to what God has done. Like most of the nine it is directed to God (contrast the idol-worship of Psa 106:19, #8), but where the others leave the spring of worship unstated, here it is named. The bearer is universal ('all the earth'), shared with Psa 96:9 (#4), yet only here is that universal homage tied to God's deeds as its cause and welded to singing praise.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'worship' (shachah) - 'all the nations you have made shall come and worship before you.' Type (102) is action: a doing, the nations' act of homage. Source (103) is absent: no named spring is booked - the reading reports the coming worship, not its cause, though the surrounding verses rehearse God's greatness and wondrous works (v10). Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the nations as such. Bearer (105) is 'all the nations' (inferred, to_span 284378): the interior in view is that of the peoples God has made - the whole gentile world drawn to homage. Operation (106) is 'worship': the event is the nations' bending before God. Target (107) is 'before God' (inferred, to_span 284378): the homage is aimed at the LORD. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) is 'paired with glorifying his name' (inferred, to_span 284378): the worship is welded to the glorifying of God's name - bowing and honouring the name move together. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v9 'All the nations... shall come and WORSHIP (shachah) before you' - the homage of the peoples, worship as the destiny of the nations. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture the nations are to hold. Locus (116) is external:god - the worship's reference-point is God, directed outward to him. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, all the nations God has made come and bow before him, their worship welded to the glorifying of his name - homage read as the appointed destiny of the peoples, directed wholly to God.
narratives.story: In the middle of a personal prayer for help, the psalmist lifts his eyes to a far horizon: one day all the nations God has made will come and bow before him. Worship here is the destiny of the whole world - not just Israel, but every people, drawn in to do homage. The bowing comes joined to honouring God's name; the peoples kneel and give glory in one movement. The passage does not say what will finally bring them or what will follow; it simply sees the nations converging on God, giving him the reverence that is his due. It is a picture of homage as the appointed end of all peoples - the world, one day, on its knees before the God who made it.
narratives.variation_note: Second of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings. Its distinctive is the bearer and horizon: 'all the nations' - the whole gentile world - coming to bow, worship read as the appointed DESTINY of the peoples, welded to glorifying God's name. It shares its universal reach with Psa 66:4 (#1) and Psa 96:9 (#4), but unlike #1 it books no source, and unlike the congregational readings (#3, #6, #7) its bearer is the nations rather than the gathered covenant people. It stands wholly apart from the idol-worship of Psa 106:19 (#8).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'kneel' (barak) - 'let us kneel before the LORD, our Maker.' Type (102) is action: a doing, the bodily bending of the knee. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the summons to kneel, not its cause, though the surrounding verses ground it in God's making of earth, sea, and mountains (v4-5). Seat (104) resolves to none: the kneeling is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the whole self, the frame bent rather than a faculty engaged. Bearer (105) is 'the worshippers' (inferred, to_span 285492): the interior in view is the gathered congregation - the 'us' summoned to come and bow. Operation (106) is 'kneel': the event is the bending of the knee before God. Target (107) is 'before the LORD our Maker' (inferred, to_span 285492): the kneeling is aimed at God as Maker - the creature bending before the one who formed it. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the call stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree of the kneeling is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding the reading registers fastens the kneeling to God as its reference-point - the knee bent toward no other. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v6 'let us KNEEL (barak) before the LORD our Maker!' - the kneeling of worship, creatures before their creator. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the worshipping people. Locus (116) here records 'paired with bowing down': the reading places the kneeling alongside its sibling posture of bowing, one of the three body-acts of v6 (worship, bow down, kneel) that together form a single summons. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the gathered people are called to bend the knee before the LORD their Maker, the kneeling fastened to God alone and set beside its companion postures of worship and bowing - the creature's body lowered before its creator as one movement of a threefold call.
narratives.story: This psalm calls the people to come and worship, and it does so with three linked pictures of the body: worship, bow down, and kneel. Kneeling is the plain bending of the knee, and here it is set before God named as Maker - the one whose hand holds the depths of the earth and who formed the dry land. The point is the relation it enacts: creatures going down on their knees before the one who made them. The kneeling belongs to God alone, turned toward no other, and it comes as part of a single summons alongside bowing low - three gestures of one act of reverence. The passage does not explain what stirs the people to kneel or what comes of it; it simply calls them, as made things, to bend before their Maker.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'bow down' (kara) - the bending of the body low in reverence, distinct from the kneeling (barak) and the worship (shachah) named alongside it in the same verse. Type (102) is action: a doing, the frame bent down. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the call to bow, not its cause, though v4-5 ground it in God's creation. Seat (104) resolves to none: the bowing is not lodged in an inner organ; it grips the whole frame, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is 'the worshippers' (inferred, to_span 285491): the interior in view is the gathered congregation summoned in v6. Operation (106) is 'bow down': the event is the low bending of the body. Target (107) is 'before God' (inferred, to_span 285491): the bowing is aimed at God. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the call stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the bowing to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v6 'let us WORSHIP and BOW DOWN (kara)' - the bending of the body in reverence, humility before the Maker. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the worshipping people. Locus (116) here records 'paired with worshipping': the reading places the bowing alongside its sibling act of worship (shachah), part of the threefold summons of v6. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the gathered people are called to bow the body low before God, the bowing fastened to him alone and set beside worship and kneeling - one of three distinct body-acts (kara here, shachah, barak) that the verse holds together yet does not collapse, each naming a facet of the creature's reverence before its Maker.
narratives.story: In the same call to worship, a second word for the body's reverence appears: to bow down low. It sits between two others - the word for worship and the word for kneeling - and the psalm deliberately holds all three together without merging them, as if to say the whole body has its ways of showing awe. This bowing is the low bending of the frame in humility, turned toward God alone. Like its companions it belongs to the Maker and to no other. The passage does not trace what moves the people to bow or what follows from it; it simply gathers them into one act of reverence made of several gestures, the body brought low before the God who formed the earth and sea.

narratives.story: At the centre of this call to worship stands the lead invitation: come, let us worship and bow down. This is the governing act of homage, and the two gestures that follow it - bowing low and kneeling - are the body's ways of carrying it out. It is directed to God alone, named here as the Maker, and it gathers the whole congregation into reverence before him. The passage carefully keeps the three motions distinct rather than blurring them into one word, as if each adds something to the picture of a people prostrate before their God. It does not say what stirs the worship or what it brings about; it simply issues the summons - the covenant people, made by God's own hands, coming to bow before him.
narratives.variation_note: Third of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings, and one of three body-postures held together in Psa 95:6 (with kneel/barak #H1288:kneel#1 and bow-down/kara #H3766:bowdown#1). Its distinctive is that here worship is the LEAD verb of a threefold summons by the gathered covenant congregation before their Maker - the governing act the sibling gestures enact. It differs from the universal readings (#1 all the earth, #2 all nations, #4 all the earth) in that its bearer is the assembled worshipping people, and from #8 (Psa 106:19) which turns the same verb toward an idol. The finding is that the passage refuses to collapse worship, bowing, and kneeling into one - their distinction is preserved.

narratives.story: This psalm calls every land to bring an offering and come into God's courts, and its charge to the world is to worship the Lord in the splendour of holiness. Worship here is homage offered to a God approached in beauty and awe. And it does not stand alone: the very next breath tells all the earth to tremble before him. So the bowing carries a shudder in it - reverence and fear together, the world brought low before a holiness that is glorious and frightening at once. The passage does not say what first moves the earth to worship or what comes of it; it simply summons all peoples to bow before the holy God, and to do so trembling.
narratives.variation_note: Fourth of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings. Its distinctive is the colouring by awe: the worship is set 'paired with trembling before him' and offered 'in the splendour of holiness' - homage shot through with fear. Its bearer, 'all the earth', it shares with #1 (Psa 66:4) and the universal reach of #2 (Psa 86:9), but unlike #1 it books no source, and unlike the congregational readings (#3, #6, #7) its horizon is the whole world. Against the reverent-and-glad tones elsewhere, this reading foregrounds the trembling that worship of a holy God carries.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'worshipers of images' (abad) - those who serve carved gods. Read at full weight, this is the family's service-word in its dark form: the same verb that names service to God here names devotion to idols. Type (102) is status: not a single act but a standing condition - what these persons are, image-servers. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked for the idolatry - the reading reports the status and its ruin, not its cause. Seat (104) resolves to none: the idol-service is not lodged in a named inner organ; it is the persons' condition, not a faculty's malfunction. Bearer (105) is 'idolaters' (inferred, to_span 285687): the interior in view is that of the image-servers, those who make their boast in worthless idols. Operation (106) is 'worship images': the event is the serving of carved gods. Target (107) is 'instead of God' (inferred, to_span 285687): the devotion is aimed at images in God's place - service misdirected, given to the worthless. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked - though the shaming is registered elsewhere in the row. Coupling (112) here records 'internal:ib-state': the binding fastens the idol-service to an inner condition - the devotion rooted within, a state of the heart bent on images. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v7 'All WORSHIPERS (abad) of images are put to shame' - those who serve carved gods, false devotion exposed and confounded. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the idolaters' interior. Locus (116) here records 'paired with being put to shame': the reading places the idol-service alongside its outcome - the shame that overtakes it, the false devotion confounded before the exalted LORD. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the idolaters serve carved images in God's place, their devotion an inner condition bent on the worthless - and the reading welds that service to its ruin, for the image-servers are put to shame; service misdirected ends in confusion before the God who is most high over all.
narratives.story: Not all worship in this psalm is rightly aimed. Here the spotlight falls on people who serve images - who pour their devotion into carved idols and boast in things that are worthless. It is the very same kind of service that elsewhere is given to God, but bent toward false gods, and the passage looks at it squarely rather than looking away. This is not a passing mistake but a settled condition of the heart: what these people are, image-servers, their devotion lodged inside them and fixed on the wrong thing. And the passage ties that misdirected service straight to its end - they are put to shame. Before the God who is most high over all the earth, the idols prove empty and their servants are left confounded. Service given to the worthless comes to nothing but disgrace.

Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the command, not its cause, though it follows the melting of the mountains and the shaming of idolaters (v5-7). Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the whole self. Bearer (105) is 'the gods / all' (inferred, to_span 285692): the interior in view is that of every rival power - the 'gods' themselves commanded to bow, homage demanded of all that might contend with God. Operation (106) is 'worship': the event is the bending of every power before God. Target (107) is 'God' (inferred, to_span 285692): the homage is aimed at the LORD, exalted far above all gods (v9). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the command stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the worship to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v7 'WORSHIP (shachah) him, all you gods!' - the call for every power to bow to God, worship due him alone. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing obligation laid on all powers. Locus (116) here records 'paired with the idolaters shamed': the reading places this command to worship alongside the shaming of the image-servers in the same verse - the two set in stark contrast, false devotion confounded while all powers are summoned to the true. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, every rival power is commanded to bow to God, the homage fastened to him alone - and the reading sets this true worship directly against the shamed idol-service of the same verse, so that the very moment the image-servers are confounded, all gods are called to their knees before the LORD who is exalted above them.
narratives.story: In a single verse the psalm holds two opposite things side by side. First, those who serve images are put to shame; then, in the same breath, comes a command that turns everything upward: worship him, all you gods. Every power that might set itself against God - every so-called god - is summoned to bow to him alone. Homage here is not offered but demanded, and it is owed to the LORD who is lifted far above all rivals. The passage deliberately places the true worship right next to the collapse of the false: at the very moment the idol-servers are disgraced, all powers are called to their knees. Worship, it insists, belongs to God alone, and nothing that pretends to rival him can hold its ground.
narratives.variation_note: Fifth of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings, and paired in Psa 97:7 with the idol-service of #H5647:worshiper#1. Its distinctive is the bearer: 'all you gods' - homage demanded of every rival POWER, not offered by the covenant people or the nations. It differs from the congregational readings (#3, #6, #7) and the universal-earth readings (#1, #2, #4) in whom it addresses, and it is set in deliberate contrast to the shamed idolaters of the same verse - true worship called for at the very moment false devotion is confounded. The finding is the head-to-head of true and false devotion within one verse.

Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the command, not its cause, though it follows the LORD's enthronement and holiness (v1-3). Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the whole self. Bearer (105) is 'the worshippers' (inferred, to_span 285825): the interior in view is that of the congregation called to exalt and bow. Operation (106) is 'worship': the event is the bending before God at his footstool. Target (107) is 'at God's footstool' (inferred, to_span 285825): the homage is aimed at God, located at the place of his presence - the footstool of the enthroned King. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the call stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the worship to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v5 'WORSHIP (shachah) at his footstool!' - the prostration before God, reverence at his holy place. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the worshipping people. Locus (116) here records 'paired with exalting God': the reading places the worship alongside the summons to exalt the LORD our God (v5) - bowing and lifting-high held together, the creature going low as it declares God high. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the congregation is called to bow at God's footstool, the homage fastened to him and set beside the exalting of his name - worship at the place of the enthroned King's presence, the people going down before the God they lift up as holy.
narratives.story: The psalm opens with God reigning, enthroned in majesty while the peoples tremble, and then it turns to the worshippers with a charge: exalt the Lord our God, and worship at his footstool. To worship here is to bow at the place of God's presence - at the footstool of the King who sits enthroned above. And notice how two motions belong together: the people lift God high with their words even as they go low before him with their bodies. Declaring him exalted and bowing at his feet are one act of reverence. The passage does not explain what first moves them to worship or what it brings about; it simply calls the congregation down before the holy God, into the posture that fits creatures at the footstool of their King.
narratives.variation_note: Sixth of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings, and the first of two within Psa 99 (with #7 at v9). Its distinctive is the place: worship 'at his footstool,' the presence of the enthroned King, welded to the summons to exalt God. It differs from the universal-earth and all-nations readings (#1, #2, #4) in that its bearer is the gathered congregation, and from its twin #7, where the same refrain is repeated but relocated to God's 'holy mountain' - the doubled call across one psalm, footstool and mountain, being itself the finding.

Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the whole self. Bearer (105) is 'the worshippers' (inferred, to_span 285854): the interior in view is the congregation, again called to exalt and bow. Operation (106) is 'worship': the event is the bending before God at his holy mountain. Target (107) is 'at God's holy mountain' (inferred, to_span 285854): the homage is aimed at God, located now at Zion, the holy hill - a shift from the footstool of v5. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the call stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the worship to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v9 'and WORSHIP (shachah) at his holy mountain' - the reverent worship at Zion, homage to the holy God. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the worshipping people. Locus (116) here records 'paired with exalting God': as at v5, the reading sets the worship beside the summons to exalt the LORD our God - bowing and lifting-high held together. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the congregation is called a second time to bow, now at God's holy mountain, the homage fastened to him and again set beside the exalting of his name - the repeated refrain of v5 relocated from footstool to Zion, closing the psalm as it turned, with the people going low before the God they declare thrice holy.
narratives.story: The psalm that began with God enthroned closes by repeating its earlier call, with one change. Where the middle of the psalm had said worship at his footstool, the ending says worship at his holy mountain - the same charge, now pointing to Zion, God's holy hill. Twice over the people are told to exalt the Lord and bow before him, and both times the two motions move together: they lift God high with their praise and go low before him with their bodies. The repetition is not accidental; the doubled call frames the psalm, footstool and mountain marking the same reverence at the place of God's presence. The passage does not say what stirs the worship or what follows; it simply brings the congregation down a second time before the God it names, again and again, as holy.
narratives.variation_note: Seventh of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings, and the twin of #6 within Psa 99. The two are a deliberate pair: v5 'worship at his footstool' and v9 'worship at his holy mountain' - the same refrain, same bearer (the congregation), same welding to the summons to exalt God, but relocated from footstool to Zion. The difference is the place of homage, and the repetition itself frames the psalm. Both differ from the universal readings (#1, #2, #4) in bearer, and stand wholly apart from the idol-worship of #8.

Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the command, not its cause. Seat (104) resolves to none: the service is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the whole self. Bearer (105) is 'the worshippers' (inferred, to_span 268783): the interior in view is that of all the earth (v1), the congregation called to make a joyful noise. Operation (106) is 'serve': the event is the serving of God. Target (107) is 'the LORD with gladness' (inferred, to_span 268783): the service is aimed at the LORD, and its object carries the note of gladness - service and joy fused in the target itself. Manner (108) is none as a booked row: no separate mode is filed, though the gladness already coloured into the target functions as the spirit of the act. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the service to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v2 'SERVE (abad) the LORD with gladness!' - the glad service of God, worship as joyful obedience. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the worshipping people. Locus (116) here records 'paired with gladness and singing': the reading places the service alongside the gladness of v2 and the singing that follows ('come into his presence with singing') - service, joy, and song moving as one. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, all the earth is called to serve the LORD, the service fastened to God and welded to gladness and song - worship here as joyful obedience, service that is not grim duty but glad approach, the whole congregation coming before God's presence with singing.
narratives.story: This is a psalm of pure thanksgiving, and its charge is simple and bright: serve the Lord with gladness, come into his presence with singing. Service here is not grim duty but glad approach - the joy is built right into it, inseparable from the serving itself. All the earth is called to make a joyful noise and then to serve, and serving, gladness, and song all move together as one thing. The passage does not say what first stirs this joy or what it yields; it simply summons the whole congregation to come before God happily, singing as they serve. This is worship at its most unclouded: obedience that is also delight, a people glad to belong to the God who made them.
narratives.variation_note: Third of four 'serve' (abad) readings. Its distinctive is JOY: service welded to gladness and singing, worship as glad obedience rather than grim duty. It differs from Psa 2:11 (#1), where service is the rebel kings' submission under fear; from Psa 22:30 (#2), where it is generational service carried by unborn posterity; and starkly from Psa 106:36 (#4), the descent reading of service turned to idols. Where #1 is coloured by dread, this reading is coloured by gladness - the same act of serving God, but in a wholly different spirit.

Here worship is rendered by the service-verb abad, worship as service given. Type (102) is action: a doing, the peoples' act of service. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the gathering-to-serve, not its cause, though it rests on God's looking down to free the prisoners (v19-20). Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the peoples as such. Bearer (105) is 'peoples and kingdoms' (inferred, to_span 268998): the interior in view is that of the assembled nations - whole peoples and their kingdoms converging. Operation (106) is 'worship / serve': the event is the nations' gathering to serve God. Target (107) is 'the LORD' (inferred, to_span 268998): the service is aimed at the LORD. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the worship to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v22 'and kingdoms, to WORSHIP (abad) the LORD' - the nations gathering to serve God, worship widened to all peoples. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the assembled peoples. Locus (116) here records 'paired with the gathering of peoples': the reading places the worship alongside the convergence of nations - the assembling and the serving held together, worship as the purpose that draws the peoples in. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, peoples and kingdoms gather to serve the LORD, the worship fastened to God and welded to the very gathering that brings them - service widened past Israel to all nations, the assembling of the peoples finding its purpose in the homage they come to give.
narratives.story: Written for a generation yet to be born, this psalm looks ahead to a day of gathering. Peoples and whole kingdoms will come together, it says, for one purpose: to worship the Lord. Worship here is service rendered to God, and it is what draws the nations in - the assembling and the serving are one, the crowds converging precisely in order to bow. What began as Israel's God becomes the God whom all peoples come to serve. The passage does not trace what stirs this gathering or what comes of it beyond the homage itself; it simply sees the nations streaming together, kingdom after kingdom, to give God the service that is his due. It is a vision of worship widened to the whole world, the peoples finding their meeting-point at the feet of the one Lord.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'worship' (shachah) - 'they made a calf in Horeb and worshiped a metal image.' Read at full weight and without valence-filtering, this is the family's worship-word turned to its darkest use: the same bowing that belongs to God given to a cast idol. Type (102) is action: a doing, the bending before the metal image. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked for the calf-worship - the reading reports the act and its exchange, not its cause. Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in a named inner organ; it is the fathers' act, not a faculty's working. Bearer (105) is 'the fathers' (inferred, to_span 269630): the interior in view is that of the wilderness generation at Horeb - the ancestors who forgot God their Saviour (v21). Operation (106) is 'worship': the event is the bowing before the molten calf. Target (107) is 'a metal image' (inferred, to_span 269630): the homage is aimed at a cast idol - worship misdirected, the bending given to a thing that eats grass (v20). Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'internal:ib-state': the binding fastens the calf-worship to an inner condition - the idolatry rooted within, a state of the heart bent on the image. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v19 'and WORSHIPED (shachah) a metal image' - the calf-worship at Horeb, the exchange of the living God for an idol. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the wilderness generation's interior. Locus (116) here records 'paired with exchanging the glory': the reading places the worship alongside v20's exchange - 'they exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass'; the bowing and the swap are one act, homage given to the idol being the trading-away of God's glory. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the fathers at Horeb bow before a molten calf, the idolatry an inner condition of the heart - and the reading welds that worship to the exchange it enacts, the glory of the living God traded for the image of a grass-eating ox; worship here is not homage rightly aimed but the whole family's central act inverted, the bending that God alone deserves poured out on a thing of metal.
narratives.story: This is the family's central act shown at its worst. At Horeb, the very people God had just rescued from Egypt made a calf of metal and bowed down to it. The same reverence that belongs to the living God was poured out on a lump of cast metal - the passage does not soften it or explain it away, but reports it plainly and calls it what it is. And it names the horror underneath: in bowing to the calf they exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass. The bowing and the trade are one and the same thing. This idolatry was not a slip of the moment but something lodged in the heart, a devotion turned inside out. Worship, which should lift a person toward God, here drags a whole people down to a statue - the highest act given to the lowest thing, and the true God forgotten.
narratives.variation_note: Eighth of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings, and the lone DESCENT among them. Every other reading of this verb bows to God - the earth (#1, #4), the nations (#2), the congregation (#3, #6, #7), all powers (#5); here alone the same act is turned to a cast idol at Horeb, its target a 'metal image' rather than the LORD, its coupling an inner idolatrous condition, welded to the exchange of God's glory for an ox that eats grass. The difference is total and it is the finding: worship's very form inverted, the bending God deserves given to a thing of metal. It reads as the dark mirror of the true-worship readings.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'serve' (abad) - 'They served their idols, which became a snare to them.' Read at full weight, this is the family's service-word in its dark form: service, which should be given to God, here rendered to idols. Type (102) is action: a doing, the serving of false gods. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked for the idol-service - the reading reports the act and its ruin, not its cause. Seat (104) resolves to none: the service is not lodged in a named inner organ; it is the fathers' act, not a faculty's malfunction. Bearer (105) is 'the fathers' (inferred, to_span 269722): the interior in view is that of the wilderness and settlement generations who mingled with the nations and adopted their gods. Operation (106) is 'serve': the event is the serving of idols. Target (107) is 'their idols' (inferred, to_span 269722): the service is aimed at false gods - devotion misdirected, given to the very things that would trap them. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked - though the snaring is registered elsewhere in the row. Coupling (112) here records 'internal:ib-state': the binding fastens the idol-service to an inner condition - the devotion rooted within, a state of the heart bent on false gods. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v36 'They SERVED (abad) their idols, which became a snare to them' - the idolatry that trapped the people. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing trait of the people's interior across this psalm of national sin. Locus (116) here records 'paired with the idols that snared them': the reading places the service alongside its outcome - the idols becoming a snare; the serving and the trap are one, the devotion given to false gods closing like a net around those who gave it. narratives.story: This long confession of national sin reaches one of its lowest points here: the people served their idols, and those idols became a trap for them. Service that belongs to God was handed instead to false gods - and the passage does not gloss over it but sets down plainly what it cost. The devotion was not skin-deep; it was lodged in the heart, a settled bent toward the wrong gods. And the terrible irony is built right in: the very idols they served closed around them like a snare. Instead of setting them free, their worship caught them and held them fast, dragging them into deeper ruin - child sacrifice, bloodshed, a polluted land. Service is meant to bind a person to God; turned toward idols, it binds them instead to the things that will destroy them.
narratives.variation_note: Fourth of four 'serve' (abad) readings, and the DESCENT among them. The other three serve God - the rebel kings under fear (#1, Psa 2:11), the unborn posterity (#2, Psa 22:30), the glad congregation (#3, Psa 100:2); here alone service is turned to idols, its target 'their idols,' its coupling an inner idolatrous condition, welded to the snare those idols became. The difference is the target and its ruin: the same act of serving, rightly given to God, here misdirected and self-entrapping. It is the dark counterpart of the three God-directed service readings.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'brought low' (shachach) - 'When they are diminished and brought low through oppression, evil, and sorrow.' Read at full weight, this is the family's low-bending word in its passive, afflictive form: not the bowing of homage but the abasement forced on a people by hardship. Type (102) is state: not a chosen act but a condition the people fall into - diminished, bowed down, brought low. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the state, not an inner cause, tracing it instead to outward oppression. Seat (104) resolves to none: the abasement is not lodged in a named inner organ; it grips the people as such, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is 'the people' (inferred, to_span 270007): the interior in view is that of a community once multiplied and blessed (v38), now diminished and pressed down. Operation (106) is 'be brought low': the event is the passive sinking of the people under affliction. Target (107) is 'through oppression' (inferred, to_span 270007): the reading marks the means by which they are lowered - oppression, evil, and sorrow the instruments that bend them. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked - though the psalm goes on to their raising-up (v41). Coupling (112) here records 'internal:ib-state': the binding fastens the abasement to an inner condition - the being-brought-low a state of the whole inner person, not merely an outward loss. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v39 'When they are diminished and BROUGHT LOW (shachach)' - the abasement of the people through affliction. Role (115) is characteristic: read as a standing condition, the low estate the afflicted fall into. Locus (116) here records 'paired with sorrow': the reading places the abasement alongside the sorrow of v39 - the being-brought-low welded to grief, the outward diminishing and the inward sorrow held together. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the people are pressed down and diminished by oppression, evil, and sorrow, the abasement an inner condition welded to grief - the family's low-bending here not homage freely given but a state suffered, the whole inner person bowed under affliction until, beyond this reading, God raises the needy up.
narratives.story: This part of the psalm turns the low, bent posture into something suffered rather than offered. A people who had been fruitful and multiplied, blessed and increased, are now diminished and brought low - pressed down by oppression, by evil, by sorrow. This is not a bowing they chose in reverence; it is an abasement forced on them by hard circumstance. And it reaches inside: the passage does not treat it as mere outward loss but as a low estate of the whole inner person, bound up with grief. Being brought low and being filled with sorrow are one condition here. The passage sets down the affliction honestly, without hurrying past it - though the psalm as a whole will go on to tell how God lifts the needy out of their misery. For this moment, though, the picture is simply a people bowed under the weight of trouble.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'being' (kabod) - 'I will sing and make melody with all my being!' The word is 'glory,' here read as the whole weighty self, the innermost person engaged in praise. Type (102) is faculty: not an act or a state but the inner capacity itself - the 'being' as the seat and instrument of worship, the whole self as the organ of praise. Source (103) is absent: no separate interior spring is booked - the reading reports the self given over to praise, not an origin behind it. Seat (104) resolves to none: though 'being/glory' names the deep self, the reading does not treat it as one located organ - it is the whole person engaged, not a single faculty switched on. Bearer (105) is 'the psalmist' (inferred, to_span 270083): the interior in view is David's, whose heart is steadfast (v1) and who will awake the dawn with song. Operation (106) is 'worship with the whole self': the event is the total engagement of the being in praise - nothing held back. Target (107) is 'toward God' (inferred, to_span 270083): the praise is aimed at God. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent as booked rows: no separate degree, narrowing, or outcome is filed, though the 'all my being' already signals totality within the sense. Coupling (112) here records 'internal:ib-state': the binding fastens the praise to an inner condition - worship rooted within, the whole self as a state given to God. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v1 'with all my BEING (kabod)!' - the whole self, glory and soul, engaged in praise, nothing held back. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing bearing of the worshipper who withholds nothing. Locus (116) here records 'paired with the heart and singing': the reading places the being alongside the steadfast heart of v1 and the singing that pours from it - the deep self, the heart, and the song held together as one act of praise. The full process: from no booked source and no single organ-seat, the psalmist gives his whole being to God in praise, the deep weighty self engaged with nothing held back - worship here not a posture of the body but the total self poured out in song, the being welded to the steadfast heart and the melody, an inner state wholly turned toward God.
narratives.story: Where much of this family shows the body bowing, this line shows the whole inner self singing. My heart is steadfast, the psalmist says, and I will sing and make melody with all my being. The word he uses points to the weightiest, deepest part of a person - the true self, the glory of who he is - and he throws all of it into praise. Nothing is held back. This is worship not as a gesture of the hands or knees but as the entire inner person given over to God in song. His steadfast heart, his deepest self, and the melody that pours out of him are all one thing here. The passage does not trace where the impulse comes from or what it produces; it simply shows a man wholly awake, ready to wake the dawn itself, pouring the whole of himself toward God.

Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the resolve to go and bow, not its cause, though it rests on the search for a dwelling place for the LORD (v4-5). Seat (104) resolves to none: the worship is not lodged in an inner organ; it is held by the whole self. Bearer (105) is 'the people' (inferred, to_span 272979): the interior in view is that of the pilgrim community resolving to go up to God's dwelling. Operation (106) is 'worship': the event is the bending before God at his footstool. Target (107) is 'at God's footstool' (inferred, to_span 272979): the homage is aimed at God, located at the place of his presence - the footstool at the ark's resting place. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the resolve stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the worship to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v7 'Let us go to his dwelling place; let us WORSHIP (shachah) at his footstool!' - the operation of homage: the people bowing at the place of God's presence. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the pilgrim people. Locus (116) here records 'paired with the resting-place of the ark': the reading places the worship alongside the ark's resting place (v8) - the bowing bound to the location of God's presence, homage at the very spot where the ark comes to rest. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the pilgrim people resolve to go to God's dwelling and bow at his footstool, the homage fastened to God and welded to the ark's resting place - worship here as pilgrimage, the movement toward the found dwelling finding its end in the bending down at the place where God's presence rests.
narratives.story: This psalm remembers the long search for a home for the ark of God, and here that search turns into an invitation: let us go to his dwelling place, let us worship at his footstool. Worship here is the goal of a journey - the people setting out toward the place where God's presence rests, in order to bow down there. The bowing is tied to that very spot, the resting place of the ark, so that the pilgrimage and the homage are of a piece: they travel precisely in order to kneel where God has come to dwell. The passage does not explain what first stirs them to go or what follows their arrival; it simply captures the resolve - a people on their way to God's house, eager to bow at his feet in the place he has chosen to rest.
narratives.variation_note: Ninth of nine 'worship' (shachah) readings. Its distinctive is pilgrimage: worship as the goal of a journey to God's dwelling, welded to the ark's resting place, the people going up precisely to bow at his footstool. It shares the 'footstool' locale with Psa 99:5 (#6) but is set within the search for the ark's home rather than a call to a gathered congregation, and its bearer is the pilgrim community. It differs from the universal readings (#1, #2, #4) in horizon and from the idol-worship of #8 in its object - here homage is rightly aimed at God's chosen dwelling.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'bow down' (shachah) - here in a forbidden form: 'you shall not bow down to a foreign god.' Read at full weight, this is the family's homage-word placed under a ban: the very bending that God rightly claims, forbidden when aimed at a foreign god. Type (102) is action: a doing, the bending of the body - here the act that must not be done. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the prohibition, not an inner cause. Seat (104) resolves to none: the bowing is not lodged in a named inner organ; it is the person's act, the whole self bending. Bearer (105) is 'you (Israel)' (inferred, to_span 283879): the interior in view is Israel's, addressed directly by God in the divine speech of v8-9. Operation (106) is 'bow down': the event is the bending before a god - the forbidden homage. Target (107) is 'to a foreign god' (inferred, to_span 283879): the bowing, were it done, would be aimed at a strange god - homage misdirected, the very thing forbidden. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the ban stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) is 'paired with the ban on the strange god' (inferred, to_span 283879): the binding registered welds the bowing to the prohibition itself - 'there shall be no strange god among you'; the forbidden homage and the forbidden god are one demand. Prohibition (113) is absent as a booked row: strikingly, though the whole reading is a negated command, no separate prohibition-flag is filed - the forbidding is carried within the sense and the coupling rather than marked as its own dimension, so the ban lives in what is said, not in a separate tag. Discovery (114) names it: v9 'you shall not BOW DOWN (shachah) to a foreign god' - the worship forbidden, exclusive allegiance the first demand. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing claim on Israel's allegiance. Locus (116) is external:god - the bowing's reference-point is a god (here a false one), directed outward; the homage points away from the true God to a foreign one, which is precisely why it is banned. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, Israel is forbidden to bow to a foreign god, the prohibited homage welded to the ban on the strange god itself - the family's own act of worship placed under interdiction the moment its object is wrong; exclusive allegiance is the first demand, and the very bending that God claims is forbidden the instant it turns toward another.
narratives.story: In this psalm God himself speaks to his people, and one of his first demands is a sharp prohibition: there shall be no strange god among you, and you shall not bow down to a foreign god. The bowing in question is the same act of homage that rightly belongs to God - but here it is placed under a ban the moment its object changes. To bow to a foreign god is forbidden precisely because worship is meant for the true God alone. The prohibition and the forbidden god are a single demand: no strange god, and no bending toward one. What God asks first is undivided loyalty - that the reverence owed to him never be turned toward another. The passage does not dwell on motives or consequences; it simply draws the line, forbidding the very gesture of worship the instant it points the wrong way.
narratives.variation_note: First of two 'bow down' (shachah) readings, and the FORBIDDEN one. Here the homage is placed under a ban - 'you shall not bow down to a foreign god' - its target a strange god, welded to the prohibition on the foreign god itself; notably the prohibition dimension is not separately flagged, the forbidding living in the sense and coupling. It is the mirror image of Psa 138:2 (#2), where the same verb names the psalmist's rightful bowing toward God's holy temple. The two readings share one word and one gesture but stand at opposite moral poles: forbidden homage to a false god versus commended homage to the true - and that opposition is the finding.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'bow down' (shachah) - 'I bow down toward your holy temple.' Type (102) is action: a doing, the psalmist's act of homage. Source (103) is absent: no interior spring is booked - the reading reports the bowing, not its cause, though it flows from thanks for God's steadfast love and faithfulness (v2). Seat (104) resolves to none: the bowing is not lodged in a named inner organ; it is the person's act, the whole self bending. Bearer (105) is 'the psalmist' (inferred, to_span 273316): the interior in view is David's, who gives thanks with his whole heart and sings God's praise before the gods (v1). Operation (106) is 'bow down': the event is the psalmist's bending toward God's temple. Target (107) is 'toward the holy temple' (inferred, to_span 273316): the homage is aimed at God, directed toward his holy temple - the bowing oriented to the place of his presence. Manner (108) is none: no mode is marked; the report stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110), and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no separate outcome is booked. Coupling (112) here records 'external:god': the binding fastens the bowing to God as its reference-point. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: v2 'I BOW DOWN (shachah) toward your holy temple' - the prostration of worship, the body enacting the thanks. Role (115) is characteristic: a standing posture of the thankful worshipper. Locus (116) here records 'paired with giving thanks to God's name': the reading places the bowing alongside the thanks of v2 - 'and give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness'; the bending and the thanksgiving are one act, the body enacting what the heart declares. The full process: from no booked source and no organ-seat, the psalmist bows toward God's holy temple, the homage fastened to God and welded to thanksgiving - worship here as the body giving form to gratitude, the whole self bending toward the place of God's presence in answer to his steadfast love and faithfulness.
narratives.story: Full of thanks for God's steadfast love and faithfulness, the psalmist gives that gratitude a shape: he bows down toward God's holy temple. His whole heart is already praising, and now his body joins in - the bending toward the temple is the thanks made visible. Worship here is thanksgiving enacted, the posture that answers a heart overflowing with gratitude, and it is aimed squarely at God, turned toward the place of his presence. The bowing and the thanks are not two separate things but one: as he honours God's name for all his kindness, his body goes low toward the temple. The passage does not trace what first stirred the gratitude or what follows it; it simply shows a thankful man bending toward his God, the whole self bowed in answer to a love that has proved faithful.
narratives.variation_note: Second of two 'bow down' (shachah) readings, and the RIGHTFUL one. Here the homage is the psalmist's own bowing toward God's holy temple, welded to thanksgiving for God's steadfast love and faithfulness - the body enacting gratitude. It is the mirror image of Psa 81:9 (#1), where the same verb names the forbidden bowing to a foreign god. One word, one gesture, opposite poles: forbidden homage to a false god there, commended homage to the true God here. The difference in target and moral valence is the finding - the very act banned when misdirected is commended when rightly aimed.
